steps.message: I'll read RetryPolicy.cs and its test class so the mutation reasoning is grounded in the real guards, the actual pattern-match set, and the exact test methods rather than assumptions.

With RetryPolicy.cs and the three passing xUnit tests in front of me, I applied each candidate mutation against the suite by tracing it through the existing assertions and verified which survivors slip through. This is static mutation reasoning grounded in the code I just read, not a live test run. Three mutations survive and two are already killed.

Survived (real gaps):

1. Null-error guard (null-check). Line 7 `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(error)` — none of the three tests passes a null exception, so deleting the guard is undetected. No assertion covers it, so the mutant is indistinguishable from the original and survives. Fix: `Assert.Throws<ArgumentNullException>(() => policy.ShouldRetry(null!, 1))`.

2. Positive-attempt guard (boundary). Line 9 `if (attempt < 1) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(...)` is never hit because every test uses attempt 1 or 3, never zero or negative. Weakening it to `attempt < 0` changes no tested outcome, so it survives. Fix: `Assert.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>(() => policy.ShouldRetry(new TimeoutException(), 0))` to pin the zero-attempt case.

3. IOException classification (return-value / set membership). Line 19 `return error is TimeoutException or IOException` — the retryable set has two members but only TimeoutException is exercised (line 13). Dropping IOException from the pattern changes no tested outcome, so it survives — I/O failures would silently stop being retried. Fix: `Assert.True(policy.ShouldRetry(new IOException(), 1))`.

Killed (already protected — no new test needed):

- The line 14 `attempt >= 3` cap is pinned by ShouldRetry_ThirdAttempt_ReturnsFalse; mutating it to `> 3` turns that test red.
- The non-retryable default is pinned by ShouldRetry_NonTransientError_ReturnsFalse (InvalidOperationException); forcing line 19 to `return true` fails it.

So the three focused tests to add are the null error, the zero-attempt argument check, and the IOException-is-retryable case — nothing else, since the attempt-three boundary and the default-deny path are already caught.
